1: # Project Discovery Intake Protocol
2: 
3: ## Purpose
4: 
5: Define a bounded, low-technical intake that establishes *what the human actually wants* before any architecture is proposed. It exists because an unbounded planning interview either interrogates the developer indefinitely or silently replaces unanswered questions with agent assumptions and agent-preferred complexity.
6: 
7: This protocol is loaded on demand. It is not part of the static directive.
8: 
9: ---
10: 
11: ## Activation
12: 
13: Run this protocol when **any** of the following is true:
14: 
15: - The repository is greenfield: no manifest, no source directory, no commit history describing shipped behavior.
16: - The project profile contains unresolved `[e.g. ...]` placeholders in the sections that describe the product, the stack, or the commands.
17: - The project profile has no `intake-status:` line and the project has no recorded planning record.
18: 
19: **Do not run this protocol** when:
20: 
21: - `intake-status: complete` is recorded and scope has not changed.
22: - The task is Level 0 (Direct) or Level 1 (Standard) work on an existing project.
23: - The human explicitly declines and accepts the recorded assumptions path (see §C).
24: 
25: Brownfield repositories with an existing filled profile and git history are **not** greenfield. A missing `intake-status:` line alone never triggers a full interview; it resolves to `legacy-partial`.
26: 
27: ---
28: 
29: ## A. Size Class and Question Budget
30: 
31: | Size | Signal | Rounds | Max questions | Extra artifacts |
32: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
33: | `small` | One surface, solo maintainer, short-lived tool or MVP | 1 | 5 | Intake Record only |
34: | `medium` | Two to three surfaces (for example web plus API, or API plus data) | 2 | 8 | Project design profile when a UI surface exists |
35: | `large` | Three or more surfaces, or authentication plus data plus deployment, or multiple teams | 3 | 12 | Architecture specification and Decision Records |
36: 
37: Rules:
38: 
39: 1. The **human states the size**. The agent may suggest a size but must label it a suggestion and ask for confirmation.
40: 2. Persist the confirmed value as `size: small | medium | large` in the project profile, using the same machine-readable convention as `profile:` and `tracking:`.
41: 3. The budget is a **ceiling, not a target**. Stop as soon as the coverage slots in §B are satisfied. Never pad a round to reach the budget.
42: 4. If the budget is exhausted with slots still open, close the intake and record the remaining slots as owned assumptions (§C).
43: 
44: ### Round, Turn, and Question Counting
45: 
46: - A **turn** is one assistant message. A **round** is one complete pass over the unanswered slots, closed by the single "Anything to add?" invitation in §C.
47: - The `Rounds` column is a ceiling on rounds. The `Max questions` column is a ceiling on **total questions across the whole intake**, not per round.
48: - The per-turn band in §C bounds how many questions one message may carry; it never raises the total. When the remaining total is smaller than three, ask only what remains and close.
49: - Counts are asserted only when the Intake Record actually tracks them. If it does not record rounds used or questions asked, report `not tracked` and do not validate arithmetic against invented numbers.
50: 
51: ---
52: 
53: ## B. Coverage Slots
54: 
55: Walk these seven slots in order. Ask at most five questions per turn, in plain language, with technical terms second.
56: 
57: | # | Slot | The question being answered | Required? |
58: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
59: | 1 | Outcome and MVP floor | What is the smallest version that is genuinely useful? | Always |
60: | 2 | Users and success signal | Who benefits, and how will success be observed? | Always |
61: | 3 | Surfaces in scope | Which of UI, API, data store, background work, integrations are in scope? | Always |
62: | 4 | Deployment target | Where does this run: local only, managed platform, virtual server, or cloud? | Always |
63: | 5 | Existing artifacts | Do an architecture document, style guide, design system, specification, or tracker board already exist? Provide links or paths. | Always |
64: | 6 | Design inputs | If a UI surface is in scope: design-tool link, screenshots, token export, or an explicit decision to use agent defaults. | Only when slot 3 includes UI |
65: | 7 | Constraints | Required stack, deadline, budget, or compliance limits? | Always |
66: 
67: Slot guidance:
68: 
69: - Ask **outcome before technology**. Never open with a framework or hosting question.
70: - Slot 5 and slot 6 are **attachment-bearing slots**. Ask them in the context window (§D) so links, files, and screenshots can be provided.
71: - **Slot 6 Design Vibe**: If no external design link or screenshot is provided, offer the 4 curated aesthetic archetypes (`Warm Paper / Editorial`, `High-Density Fintech`, `Clean Modern SaaS`, `Dark Terminal`) or system defaults so the user selects their visual vibe upfront, avoiding an unstyled monochrome void.
72: - Accept "not sure yet" for any slot. Record it as an assumption with a proposed default rather than pressing for an answer.
73: - A slot answered earlier in the same project is never re-asked unless scope changed or new evidence invalidated it.
74: 
75: ### Product-Shape Cover Questions (SaaS-Class Requests)
76: 
77: Some intents are **product-shaped**, not feature-shaped: the request implies accounts, per-user data, and money or third-party integrations — the SaaS shape. Slot 3 answers alone do not cover the decisions those surfaces create, so when slot 3 reports **two or more surfaces**, or the request names accounts plus data plus billing or integrations, ask these five **conditional** product-shape questions (`P1`–`P5`) in the same interview, in the context window (§D). They are an extension of slot 3 and slot 7 coverage, never five extra required slots.
78: 
79: | Q | Question being answered | Why it changes architecture | Boring default if unanswered |
80: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
81: | `P1` | Who can see whose data: one account, a shared workspace, or separate tenants? | Tenant boundary and every query behind it | Single-owner scope, no sharing |
82: | `P2` | How do people get in, and who administers them: self-serve signup, invitations, SSO, admin roles? | Auth surface and role model | Invitation-only, single admin |
83: | `P3` | Does money change hands — none, one-off, or recurring — and who is the billing source of truth? | Entitlements, webhooks, reconciliation | None in the MVP floor (Later ledger) |
84: | `P4` | What runs without a human: scheduled jobs, webhooks, notifications — and what happens after repeated failure? | Background surface and retry policy | Synchronous only, no jobs |
85: | `P5` | What constraints apply: personal data, region or residency, retention, audit expectations? | Data store, hosting region, logging | Recorded assumptions only, no compliance claims |
86: 
87: Rules:
88: 
89: 1. **These are questions, not proposals.** Never answer them on the human's behalf; an unanswered slot becomes an owned `ASSUMPTION-*` record per §C, never a silent default.
90: 2. **They extend slot 3 and slot 7 coverage instead of adding required slots** — one or two per round, inside the size-class cap (§A). If the budget is reached first, close the intake with assumptions (§C) instead of extending it.
91: 3. **Never answer a product-shaped request with a stack, scaffold, generator, starter template, or `create-*` command.** Naming, choosing, installing, or announcing a technology during intake is a protocol violation: the intake's first output is questions, not files. Technology stays slot 7 and the accept-or-change proposals described above.
92: 4. **A product-shaped request never authorizes an unattended build.** It states intent only; planning, milestones, and approvals still run through `pk:plan`, `pk:tasks`, and the milestone gate.
93: 5. **Capabilities nobody asked for stay put.** Admin consoles, notification systems, and pricing tiers that do not trace to a stated requirement go to the Later ledger (§E.6), never into the MVP floor.
94: 
95: ## C. Question Protocol and Stop Contract
96: 
97: ### Round Shape
98: 
99: 1. Ask **three to five** questions per turn. One question is acceptable when the previous answer changed the picture.
100: 2. Acknowledge each accepted answer in a single line before moving on. Do not restate the whole conversation.
101: 3. For any unanswered slot, propose a **boring default** and mark it as an assumption, never as a decision.
102: 
103: ### The "Anything to Add?" Loop
104: 
105: Every round closes with exactly one open-ended invitation, asked in the context window:
106: 
107: > Anything to add — text, links, screenshots, or files? Or say "enough for now".
108: 
109: Repeat a new round only while a stop condition has not fired. Do not loop the invitation inside the same turn.
110: 
111: ### Stop Conditions
112: 
113: Stop immediately when **any** of these is true:
114: 
115: 1. All seven coverage slots are satisfied.
116: 2. The human ends intake (accept "enough for now" without friction and without a counter-proposal).
117: 3. A full round produces no new information.
118: 4. The size-class question budget is reached.
119: 
120: ### Close Contract
121: 
122: Close with a recorded Intake Record (§G) that includes:
123: 
124: - `close_reason: complete | human_stopped | no_new_info | budget_reached`
125: - The explicit list of slots that remain **unknown**, so "agreed for now" becomes an auditable fact rather than ambiguity
126: - One owned assumption record per unknown slot that affects architecture, with impact-if-wrong and a validation action
127: 
128: A closed-but-incomplete intake is a valid outcome. Refusing to proceed until every slot is answered is not.
129: 
130: ### Attachment Handling
131: 
132: - If the host cannot read an attachment, say so plainly and ask for text, a quoted excerpt, or a pasted link. **Never guess the content of an unreadable attachment.**
133: - If an image or document is readable, restate in one line what was extracted (for example tokens, constraints, entity names) and confirm it before relying on it.
134: - Never request, echo, or store secrets. Continue to require `.env.example` with placeholder keys and a local `.env`.
135: 
136: ---
137: 
138: ## D. Interactive Picker Routing Rule
139: 
140: > Use a native modal picker **only** when all three conditions hold:
141: > 1. The option set is closed and has at most four entries.
142: > 2. The answer needs no attachment, no link, and no free text.
143: > 3. The agent has evidence-based grounds for the options, or the picker itself offers an explicit no-recommendation option.
144: >
145: > Otherwise ask in the **context window**.
146:

207: | Field | Required value |
208: | :--- | :--- |
209: | **Divergence ID** | `DIVERGENCE-<spec-slug>-<nnn>` - one stable ID per contradiction |

213: | **Precedence** | Exactly one of `host-doc-authority`, `decision-authority`, `unresolved` |

215: | **Owner** | The named person or role accountable for resolving the contradiction |
216: | **Next Action** | The concrete next step that closes it |

3: ## Purpose
4: Canonical visual formatting specification for telemetry cards, human-action callouts, and turn structures. Provides dual-mode rendering: **Framed Mode** (tactile ceiling-and-floor Unicode boxes, default) and **Markdown Mode** (for GitHub-style blockquote alerts), plus CLI/Terminal support across Cline, OpenCode, Aider, Cursor, VS Code, and Antigravity.
5: 
6: ---
7: 
8: ## The Single-Callout Invariant (Strict Anti-Flooding)
9: 
10: **At most ONE human callout block per turn.** Never emit multiple alert boxes or stacked callouts in the same turn (e.g. never stack `[!IMPORTANT]` with `[!TIP]`).
11: 
12: Callout types are strictly tiered by priority; only the highest applicable level fires:
13: 1. **Priority 1 (Hard Stop)**: Human sign-off, PR review ready, release authorization, or milestone boundary (`🛑ACTION REQUIRED`).
14: 2. **Priority 2 (Blocked)**: Two failed repair attempts, missing secrets/env, or execution blocker (`🚫BLOCKED`).
15: 3. **Priority 3 (Advisory Next Steps)**: Normal turn progression with numbered choices (`💡NEXT STEPS`).
16: 
17: If a higher-priority callout is active, it carries the next action; a separate advisory TIP is strictly forbidden.
18: 
19: **Precedence:** this document is canonical for callout *format*; `protocols/code-quality-gate.md` is canonical for *when-to-halt and Type A-D routing*; `protocols/setup.md` defers to both. The canonical turn-close order in both modes is **TL;DR opening → telemetry card → callout**; any workflow restating a close order must match this sequence.
20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## Universal Square Progress Bar Contract
24: 
25: Progress bars across all environments must use square geometric Unicode characters with exact 1:1 monospaced width parity:
26: - **Filled**: `■` (U+25A0)
27: - **Empty**: `□` (U+25A1)
28: - **Format**: `[■■■■■■■■□□] 80% (8/10)`
29: 
30: > [!CAUTION]
31: > **Anti-Glitch Invariant**: Shaded textured blocks (`▓`, `▒`, `░`) and solid vertical blocks (`█`) are strictly banned from progress bars because they produce font width collisions and yellow scanline rendering artifacts in IDE themes.
32: 
33: ---
34: 
35: ## Mandatory Reply Hint Contract (`👉 Reply: Type '...'`)
36: 
37: Every human callout block (`NEXT STEPS`, `ACTION REQUIRED`, `BLOCKED`, `DECISION NEEDED`, `GRILL PROBE`) across all modes must conclude with an unambiguous, single-keystroke or single-word **Reply Hint** line.
38: 
39: The developer must never wonder what to type or whether they have to write an essay:
40: - **Numbered choices**: `👉 Reply: Type '1' (or press Enter) for recommended.`
41: - **Action / Review ready**: `👉 Reply: Type 'merged' or 'done' after merging to continue.`
42: - **Blocked (mandatory stops / verification / security)**: `👉 Reply: Type 'retry' once resolved, or describe instructions.` (Skip is strictly forbidden on mandatory verification or security stops).
43: - **Blocked (waivable external prerequisites only)**: `👉 Reply: Type 'retry' once freed, or 'skip' to bypass if non-blocking.`
44: - **Decision cards**: `👉 Reply: Type 'A' for recommended, or 'you decide' to delegate.`
45:

48: ## Pre-Response Check (Compact, Per Turn)
49: 
50: Before composing the reply, answer five questions from the current execution state. This is a **reasoning step, not a mandated tool call** (see *Honest Limits* below).
51: 
52: 1. **Stop state** — genuine halt (`🛑ACTION REQUIRED` / `🚫BLOCKED`), advisory turn, or *Quiet Completion*? Silence is only correct for the third.
53: 2. **Highest applicable callout** — exactly one, at the highest applicable tier per *The Single-Callout Invariant*.
54: 3. **Concrete action + reply hint** — does it name one specific thing the human must do and close with a `👉 Reply:` line from the *Mandatory Reply Hint Contract*?
55: 4. **Retention** — is every *other* unresolved human action still recorded and unchanged?
56: 5. **Turn obligations** — TL;DR on substantive turns (informational L0 fast-path replies stay exempt), and every number traced to this turn per the *Provenance Invariant* or reported `not measured`.
57: 
58: ### Suppression Is Not Resolution
59: 
60: A lower-priority action that was not shown stays **recorded, unresolved, and unchanged** in the canonical record. The Single-Callout Invariant limits how many *boxes* a turn renders; it never discharges an obligation. Re-surface the action on the turn it becomes the highest applicable one. Never state or imply that "only one callout was shown" means the others were handled, approved, or dropped.
61: 
62: ### Reply Interpretation Is Record-Bound
63: 
64: `done`, `merged`, a bare number, `continue`, `retry`, and `skip` resolve **only the recorded action they were offered against**. They never authorize an unrelated protected action (commit, push, PR, release, deploy, rollback, scope change), never cross a milestone boundary, and never promote a Priority 2 blocker into a Priority 1 approval. Where an externally observable condition exists — PR merged, CI green, file written, value on disk — verify it in this turn before treating the action as met: a reply is a claim about the human's side of the world, not evidence for it.
65: 
66: ### Resolution Requires the Recorded Condition
67: 
68: An action is resolved only when its recorded condition is actually met and, where one exists, verified as above. Until then it stays pending across turns, compaction, and handoff. Pending actions live in the canonical record the work already requires — never in a second parallel action ledger — and that record holds no credentials, tokens, or secret values; reference the env key or secret store instead.

71: 
72: `card-style: off` / `status-cards: off` suppresses only the decorative card and advisory framing, never a genuine halt. A `🛑ACTION REQUIRED` or `🚫BLOCKED` stop still fires with its concrete action and reply hint intact, rendered in plain text when nothing decorative is shown.

75: 
76: The host cannot mechanically halt an agent, inspect a future turn, or detect a missing callout; this check is a stated discipline that any model may still under-apply, and no claim is made that it prevents measured session drift. It adds no mandatory disk read or tool call to a trivial reply. Where an existing protocol already requires reading the canonical record for current state (e.g. *STATE.md Untrusted Until Read*, `pk:checkpoint`), that read answers the check too — the check never mandates an additional one.

62: ### Reply Interpretation Is Record-Bound
63: 
64: `done`, `merged`, a bare number, `continue`, `retry`, and `skip` resolve **only the recorded action they were offered against**. They never authorize an unrelated protected action (commit, push, PR, release, deploy, rollback, scope change), never cross a milestone boundary, and never promote a Priority 2 blocker into a Priority 1 approval. Where an externally observable condition exists — PR merged, CI green, file written, value on disk — verify it in this turn before treating the action as met: a reply is a claim about the human's side of the world, not evidence for it.
65: 
66: ### Resolution Requires the Recorded Condition
67: 
68: An action is resolved only when its recorded condition is actually met and, where one exists, verified as above. Until then it stays pending across turns, compaction, and handoff. Pending actions live in the canonical record the work already requires — never in a second parallel action ledger — and that record holds no credentials, tokens, or secret values; reference the env key or secret store instead.
69: 
70: ### Cards-Off Still Communicates Genuine Halts
71: 
72: `card-style: off` / `status-cards: off` suppresses only the decorative card and advisory framing, never a genuine halt. A `🛑ACTION REQUIRED` or `🚫BLOCKED` stop still fires with its concrete action and reply hint intact, rendered in plain text when nothing decorative is shown.
73: 
74: ### Honest Limits
75: 
76: The host cannot mechanically halt an agent, inspect a future turn, or detect a missing callout; this check is a stated discipline that any model may still under-apply, and no claim is made that it prevents measured session drift. It adds no mandatory disk read or tool call to a trivial reply. Where an existing protocol already requires reading the canonical record for current state (e.g. *STATE.md Untrusted Until Read*, `pk:checkpoint`), that read answers the check too — the check never mandates an additional one.
